PullRequest.Title: sessions: reveal hierarchy guides on pane hover

Fixes #343511.

## Summary

Reveal all session/sub-session hierarchy guides while the pointer is anywhere inside the Agents sessions pane, including headers and empty space. Leaving the pane restores the quiet resting appearance while preserving existing selection and keyboard-focus guides.

- Use pane-wide CSS hover and remove redundant per-row hover tracking.
- Keep row actions and collapse controls row-local; preserve connector styling and standalone completed-chat exclusions.
- Add rendered-style regression coverage and multi-hierarchy fixtures, including compact rows and high-contrast variants.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --grep 'session chat rows' --reporter dot` — passed, 98 tests.
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --grep 'hierarchy indent/connector guides' --browser chromium --reporter dot` — passed, 16 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListFixtureUtils.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.fixture.ts` — passed.
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/sessionsList.css` — passed with three existing design-token suggestions unrelated to this change.
- Real-pointer browser checks on the production list — passed for headers, parent/child/unrelated rows, empty list space, pane padding, pointer exit, and virtualized scrolling across light, dark, and both high-contrast themes with compact and normal rows.
- Commit hygiene — passed for all five changed files.
- `npm run compile-client` — blocked by an existing Markdown extension dependency mismatch (`@vscode/markdown-editor/commands` is not exported).
- `npm run typecheck-client` — blocked by existing dependency/type errors, including missing Electron declarations; no diagnostics in the changed files.

## Manual Test

1. Open the Agents window with at least two expanded session hierarchies.
2. Hover a session row, a child row, a section header, or empty space within the sessions pane. All visible hierarchy guides should appear without revealing unrelated row controls.
3. Move outside the pane. Only the existing selected/focused hierarchy guides should remain visible.
4. Repeat with compact rows, scroll to previously offscreen sessions, and check high-contrast themes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pointer enters, traverses, and leaves a Sessions pane containing multiple expanded session/chat hierarchies
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser hover-state invalidation, selector matching, and opacity repaint must complete for guides to appear or disappear. Moving between rows keeps the pane ancestor hovered, so the new pane-wide guide selector does not require JavaScript observable updates per row.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently rendered expanded session and nested-chat rows, not total stored sessions; effective cardinality is viewport-bounded by WorkbenchObjectTree virtualization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser UI-thread style/paint path; no queue, limiter, async work, or concurrent boundary operations are involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache participates. Browser style data may be warm, but both cold and warm behavior remain bounded to rendered DOM; the CSS state applies directly to newly rendered rows.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed CSS selector and removed onMouseOver/onMouseOut observable updates directly establish the before/after UI-thread behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style/paint time depends on viewport size, theme, device, and the number of simultaneously rendered nested rows, but the object tree virtualizes the list and the connector pseudo-elements are simple borders whose opacity is intentionally changed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Pane entry/exit now repaints all visible hierarchy guides as required, while row-to-row pointer traversal removes the previous repeated observable/set/class-update path and does not add a scaling boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scrolling, collapsing, or expanding sessions while the pointer remains over the pane
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing tree virtualization renders/recycles visible rows; normal CSS matching then gives each newly rendered hierarchy guide the pane-hover opacity. No explicit iteration or follow-up notification was added by the diff.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rows entering or leaving the rendered viewport during scroll, plus visible children added by expansion; total session history does not determine DOM cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous virtualized row rendering on the UI thread; existing animation-frame coalescing for list updates is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or retained hover state exists. Recycled/new rows derive visibility from the current ancestor hover state, avoiding cache invalidation and per-row hover bookkeeping.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed selector operates on descendant rendered elements, and the list implementation is a WorkbenchObjectTree with recycled viewport rows.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of rows recycled per scroll varies with row height and viewport, but only rendered rows have DOM/pseudo-elements and participate in style/paint.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work is constant per rendered row and replaces rather than adds hover-state synchronization; there is no unbounded retention or repeated full-collection work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selection and keyboard focus preserve one or more hierarchy guides after the pointer leaves the pane
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing selection/focus events update small sets of owning session IDs, and existing renderer autoruns toggle classes on rendered rows. The diff only removes hovered-session participation from that derived state.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Deduplicated selected/focused session IDs and rendered row count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event and observable propagation on the UI thread; no asynchronous fan-out or external boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The selected/focused ID sets are transient observable state with unchanged lifecycle; the removed hovered value reduces retained and invalidated state. No positive/negative cache behavior applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed derived observable no longer reads or merges the hovered session ID, while selection/focus handling remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Multi-selection size can vary, but guide ownership is deduplicated in a Set and renderer work remains limited to currently rendered rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed code reduces observable recomputation and allocation by removing the hover ID and preserves the existing bounded selection/focus path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and traced pane hover, virtualized scrolling/rendering, and selection/focus scenarios. The production diff broadens intentional guide painting only across rendered rows while removing hotter per-row hover observable updates; no actionable performance regression or evidenced shipped-regression fix was found.
